Formulation  
Patient presents with anxiety exacerbated by persistent gastrointestinal symptoms (diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting) and a family history of bowel cancer (father deceased 10 years ago). Predisposing factors include family history and asthma. Precipitating factors include recent GI illness with ongoing symptoms causing distress and impacting work. Perpetuating factors include unresolved anxiety and ongoing physical symptoms. Protective factors include patient insight, willingness to engage in medical advice, and no current risk behaviors.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Anxiety related to gastrointestinal symptoms and cancer risk  
- Patient Goal(s): To reduce anxiety related to symptoms and family history; return to work as symptoms improve  
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor physical symptoms; provide reassurance and education regarding probable gastroenteritis and low likelihood of bowel cancer; support anxiety management  
- Actions (Patient): Monitor symptoms including fever and worsening abdominal pain; maintain hydration; avoid work until symptoms improve; seek GP review if symptoms worsen or persist beyond a few days  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide education about gastroenteritis; reassure regarding low cancer risk currently; advise on symptom monitoring and when to seek urgent care; consider mental health support if anxiety persists  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Gastroenteritis causes and management, importance of hydration, symptom monitoring, red flags for worsening illness, impact of anxiety, reassurance regarding bowel cancer risk  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing abdominal pain, presence of blood in stool or vomit, fever, persistent vomiting, significant worsening diarrhea  
- Coping Strategies: Encourage hydration, rest, symptom monitoring, seek medical care as needed; consider referral for anxiety management if required
